subject: Post-call recap: Inference capacity playbook & constraints for EverWell pilot
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Rivera <samantha.rivera@everwellhealth.com>, Victor Chen <v.chen@everwellhealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 2 Aug 2026 15:10:00 -0400
Subject: Post-call recap: Inference capacity playbook & constraints for EverWell pilot

Hi Samantha / Victor —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap of what we heard, the risks you called out, and a proposed short plan so we’re aligned before we scope the pilot. I’ve attached a one‑sheet with the bullets below.

High‑level pain & goals you shared
- User-facing triage assistant must stay under 700ms (p95) for goal flows (avg 600–1,000 tokens output).
- Tail latency (p99) currently drives support tickets — target to keep <1.4s for production.
- Throughput: baseline concurrency target is 90–120 simultaneous live sessions during peak business hours; burst to 250 for marketing spikes.
- Data residency & PHI: processing must remain in your VPC / US‑east region; audit logs retained for 1 year.
- Budget: prefer a predictable committed capacity model for monthlies with ability to burst.

Immediate technical constraints / notes (from call)
- Primary model: fine‑tuned open decoder model (approx 30–70B scale) with preference for aggressive 4‑bit quantization if accuracy remains acceptable.
- Average request length today is ~850 generated tokens; warm prefix cache for session context is critical.
- Integration: must support streaming and chunked outputs to the browser.

Proposed pilot plan (next 4 weeks)
1) Scope: 2‑week sandbox in Redwood Dedicated (US‑east) with a 3‑node warm pool (H100s) + autoscale policy to 6 nodes for bursts.
2) Metrics to instrument: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, queue depth, batch size distribution, KV cache hit rate, and cold‑start frequency.
3) Safety fallback: route to smaller 13B variant when queue depth > 160 to protect p99.
4) Data flow: VPC peering + TLS + customer KMS for key wrapping.

Ask from you for the pilot scoping
- Confirm PHI scope (which endpoints will carry PHI).
- Approve access to a representative prompt set (20–30 flows) we can use to simulate production token lengths.
- Confirm target launch window (you mentioned late Sep).

Rishi & Marissa — see inline items for architecture checks. I’ll follow with a compact capacity playbook and a cost/latency estimate.

Thanks — talk soon.

—
Olga Petrov
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555‑0198

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Inference capacity playbook & constraints for EverWell pilot

Olga —

Thank you, this is a great summary and aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side: 
- PHI: only the triage notes payload will include PHI; we need end‑to‑end encryption and customer‑side KMS.
- Latency: the 700ms p95 target is firm for the main clinician flow; for longer contextual queries (ad hoc reports) we can tolerate up to 1.8s p95.
- Model: we prefer the 30B footprint if accuracy stays within 2% of our current baseline — happy to run an eval set.
- Timeline: Sep 20–24 is still our preferred pilot window.

Next steps from our side: Victor will send the prompt set and an anonymized sample of token length distribution by Tue (Aug 4). Budget approvals are pending — we have an internal cap on committed spend that I’ll confirm by Wed. If that changes the proposal we may need a hybrid committed + burst pricing.

Also, can you confirm if Redwood can provide SOC‑style evidence (audit log samples) during the POC? We might need that for our security review.

Thanks — looking forward to the playbook.

Best,
Samantha Rivera
Head of Product, Conversational Care | EverWell Health
samantha.rivera@everwellhealth.com

Samantha / Olga —

A few engineering notes to make the pilot predictable:

1) Warm pool sizing & cache strategy- We recommend a 3x warm pool (3 nodes kept ready with loaded tokenizer + KV warm) for baseline; scale to 6 nodes on CPU / GPU metrics + queue length. For your average of ~850 tokens, KV cache hit rate will save ~35% of token compute on continued sessions.

2) Batching policy- Continuous batching with a 40–80ms batching window should keep per‑token efficiency high without adding >50ms median latency. We’ll instrument batch size percentiles and surface them in the console.

3) Quantization & accuracy tradeoffs- Start with int4 (4‑bit asymmetric) for the 30B variant; run the eval set you provide at multiple quant configs (4‑bit, q4f, int8) and capture delta vs baseline. If accuracy loss >2% we’ll fallback to mixed precision for critical flows.

4) Fallback and graceful degradation- Policy: if queue depth > 180 or average request latency >900ms for 2 consecutive minutes, route to a tuned 13B variant and tag responses with a response_quality header for traceability.

5) Observability & audit needs- We can stream anonymized audit logs for the POC and provide a SOC‑style evidence package (redacted) — will need an NDA addendum to share full examples.

I’ll run a small load test with synthetic prompts once we get the prompt set and token distribution — that will give us an early p99 estimate under your burst pattern.

—
Rishi Malhotra
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
